comparator.academicYear: Current curriculum for the Fall 2026 cohort; checked 2026-09-29
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official UvA curriculum, checked 2026-09-29, defines one complete 180-EC Medicine pathway with 60 EC in each year and no formal route. Year 1 combines four patient-centred organ-system themes, a 6-EC observation and care placement, clinical and scientific methodology, academic formation and professional development. Year 2 deepens the same themes and longitudinal formation while preserving 18 EC of genuine elective space. Year 3 continues the themes and formation, includes a 12-EC medical bachelor thesis and culminates in a 14-EC preparation-for-practice block focused on clinical reasoning, history-taking and physical examination before clerkships. The official overview confirms the normalized identity, three-year 180-EC load, Dutch language, Amsterdam UMC location and RIO code 56551. Elective space is preserved without invented content. Review on 2026-10-17 reconfirmed the same current official curriculum: all settled components, EC, 18-EC elective space and absence of a formal route are preserved. The programme overview independently supports inclusive and sustainable healthcare as target interests.

alternatives.concept: Study human health and disease through cellular biology, anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, genetics, immunity, pharmacology, laboratory methods, epidemiology and psychological influences on illness. Research design, statistics, data handling and evidence synthesis support scientific investigation. This is a biomedical and health-science response to Medicine; supervised clinical reasoning, practical medical skills and patient care remain absent.

alternatives.labelRationale: Life, health, cognition and psychology courses form the substantive curriculum, supported by research methods, data analysis, ethics and mandatory PPD. The title describes biomedical and psychological study of health and disease without implying Medicine or clinical competence.

alternatives.concept: Study illness and health behaviour through physiology, brain function, cognitive impairment, developmental and clinical psychology. Sociology and qualitative inquiry examine how institutions, inequality and meanings shape illness experience; ethical reasoning and public persuasion provide specific analytical tools for questions of inclusion and health messages. This is an academic health-science programme, without medical consultation, clinical examination or supervised patient treatment.

alternatives.labelRationale: Seventeen biomedical, cognition and psychology courses form the main curriculum. Sociology, qualitative inquiry, ethics, methods and public persuasion connect this substantial core to illness experience and social conditions. Inclusion is an application supported by these tools rather than a claim that all courses teach healthcare inclusion.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Six courses / 45 EC differ in each direction. Molecular cell biology, biochemistry, molecular pathology, infection/immunity, mechanisms of disease and laboratory work give way to perception/action, language neuroscience, social psychology, sociology, qualitative inquiry and public persuasion. This changes the priority from molecular and organ-system disease research to cognitive, psychological and social processes in health and illness.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Biomedical and brain/behaviour gateways precede all dependent courses. Cell biology, physiology, biochemistry and anatomy precede advanced pathology and pharmacology where feasible. Research Methods & Statistics precedes experimental statistics and the meta-analysis seminar. Formal prerequisites and exact planned availability pass. Data handling occurs before final-year evidence synthesis. Abnormal Psychology is placed before Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies as a useful advisory progression.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two alternatives were included sequentially. The third candidate, environmental sustainability of healthcare (18094, supported by 18123), was assessed independently. UCR offers lifecycle analysis, resource recovery, renewable technology, environmental governance and sustainability communication, but no sustained healthcare-operations, healthcare-waste/materials or sustainable clinical-service sequence. Combining enough environmental courses with health courses would produce two adjacent strands without concrete healthcare-specific contributions from all 23 non-PPD courses. It therefore does not support a complete coherent third response. Clinical care, diagnostic reasoning and treatment remain explicitly unfilled core gaps; their presence does not invalidate the two related academic responses.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both address cardiovascular, pulmonary and renal function. Human Physiology supplies normal systems physiology; it does not reproduce the patient-centred medical theme.
Infection & Immunity directly addresses immune regulation, host defence and immunopathology, an important part of the integrated regulation theme; hormonal and metabolic scope is not reproduced.

Mechanisms of Disease explicitly studies cardiovascular, pulmonary and renal pathophysiology, directly overlapping the major organ systems in this clinical theme. Clinical diagnosis and treatment progression remain absent.

This later integrated medical theme retains its own specific scope and credits. UCR biochemistry, immunity and physiology provide related scientific study but not its full patient-centred medical progression.

Lifespan Developmental Psychology includes prenatal development, birth and physical/sexual development. It offers developmental psychology rather than the complete medical and reproductive theme.

notes.text: UvA Medicine integrates organ-system science with patient placements, clinical reasoning, medical skills and professional development. These UCR programmes study biomedical disease mechanisms or health through cognition, behaviour and social experience. They do not reproduce the medical clinical sequence, supervised patient care or preparation for clerkships.
